findings.problem: After the owner reworded R1 at the checkpoint, the Phase 1d status line (01d-coverage.md:74) was made the place the skip is explained, and it says it 'states the gate outcome exactly once' and 'is the only line that states the gate outcome'. But 20-selection.md:38-41 was kept unchanged and still requires a fixed Phase 2 announce suffix ('— test-sufficiency not dispatched: no coverage artifact found' / '...none usable...') that states the same outcome a second time with different wording. The result is three per-slug wordings across three files (01d status line, 20-selection suffix, deep-review.md render note), two of which disagree about which one is authoritative. Each is pinned by its own test (STATUS_NOTE, ANNOUNCE_SUFFIX, render regex), so the contradiction is locked in rather than detected.

findings.why_it_matters: The orchestrator receives conflicting instructions about where the skip reason lives, and the required-output contract in 20-selection.md ('dispatching without the line is a defect') is exactly what live evidence showed the model does not follow on gated runs — so the spec now mandates something known not to happen.
source_window: On exit 0, carry the printed `case` forward as `$TS_GATE_CASE`, one of `present`, `no-artifact`, `none-usable`. It is an orchestrator-remembered value read from the printed JSON, like `$CONFIG_DISABLED`; never rely on a shell variable surviving the turn. `20-selection.md`'s gating paragraph consumes it in the pre-dispatch turn. `$TS_GATE_CASE` and `$TS_GATED` both start UNSET at the beginning of every invocation and every pass, so a case remembered from an earlier run or pass never carries into this one. On ANY non-zero exit (the helper refused the input, `$VC_ROOT` is empty, python is missing), leave `$TS_GATE_CASE` UNSET and continue exactly as today: the empty block still injects and the agent self-skips. A failed gate NEVER skips the lane; it fails toward dispatch, so test-sufficiency dispatches as before. This gate only decides whether one Task call happens. The `<coverage-artifacts>` block content, the shared `<diff>`/`<files>` block and every prompt template are unchanged (CRITICAL CACHE INVARIANT above). The helper receives only paths, never artifact content, and nothing it prints is ever placed in a prompt or echoed into the announce line. In `--all` (`$ALL_MODE` set) this paragraph does not run: STAGE B below is unchanged, and the per-chunk empty-block fallback remains the skip path (D-03).

**REQUIRED OUTPUT — the Phase 1d status line (diff mode only).** After the helper returns, and in this same Phase 1d turn, print exactly one Phase 1d status line as text, before any Phase 2 work starts. This line is where the user learns why `test-sufficiency` will not run, so it is required on every diff-mode deep review, and it states the gate outcome exactly once. Use this fixed wording, chosen by the case: for `no-artifact`, `✓ Phase 1d — Coverage artifacts — no coverage artifact found; test-sufficiency will not run`; for `none-usable`, `✓ Phase 1d — Coverage artifacts — coverage artifacts found but none usable for the changed files; test-sufficiency will not run`; for `present`, `✓ Phase 1d — Coverage artifacts` with no gate note. When the helper failed and the case is unset, print the `present` form, because test-sufficiency dispatches. The status line never carries a file path, an artifact name or content, the helper's JSON or a variable name; it is exactly one of the three fixed lines above. If the entry announce already printed, this status line still prints; it is the only line that states the gate outcome.

**`--all` CHUNK SCOPING — STAGE B, PER-CHUNK ASSEMBLY INSIDE SITE C (filter the block per chunk; do NOT inject repo-global AS-IS; do NOT build this block before Phase 2).** STAGE A above ran ONCE pre-Phase-2 and produced the REPO-LEVEL USABLE COVERAGE DATASET (gated, parsed coverage rows for the whole repo). It did NOT build the per-chunk block — `$CHUNK_REVIEW_FILES_i` does not exist yet. In `--all` the per-chunk dispatch loop (`$VC_ROOT/phases/review/20-dispatch-all.md` Site C) runs once per chunk and binds each chunk's prompts to that chunk's `$CHUNK_REVIEW_FILES_i` (the post-`files_to_skip_i` surviving file list), NOT the whole `$REVIEW_SET`. WHERE STAGE B RUNS (be precise — this is the whole fix): the per-chunk `<coverage-artifacts>` block for chunk `i` is ASSEMBLED INSIDE the Site C loop, AFTER `$VC_ROOT/phases/review/20-dispatch-all.md` Site C step 2 derives `$CHUNK_REVIEW_FILES_i` (`$CHUNK_REVIEW_FILES_i = $CHUNK_FILES_i` MINUS `files_to_skip_i`) and BEFORE that chunk's pure-Task fan-out turn (`$VC_ROOT/phases/review/20-dispatch-all.md` Site C step 5) — the SAME window in which `$VC_ROOT/phases/review/20-dispatch-all.md` Site C step 3 builds `$FILES_BLOCK_i`. DO NOT attempt to build this per-chunk block at STAGE A / pre-Phase-2 — there is no `$CHUNK_REVIEW_FILES_i` to filter against there, and falling back to a repo-global block would resurrect the cross-chunk leak this fix closes. HOW: for chunk `i`, take STAGE A's repo-level usable dataset and FILTER it to ONLY the coverage rows whose file is in the CURRENT chunk's `$CHUNK_REVIEW_FILES_i`; that filtered set is chunk `i`'s `<coverage-artifacts>` block. This keeps each chunk's test-sufficiency agent reporting ONLY on its own chunk's files — required because `scripts/score.py`'s `in_reviewed_set` validates against the RUN-LEVEL `$REVIEWED_UNION` (`$VC_ROOT/phases/review/20-dispatch-all.md` Site C, where `$REVIEWED_UNION` is bound), NOT the emitting chunk, so an unfiltered repo-global block would let a chunk-`i` agent emit (and survive) off-scope coverage findings for another chunk's files (duplicate / off-scope blocking findings, broken chunk isolation). BYTE CAP + REVIEWED-SET MATCH + EMPTY FALLBACK AT THIS STAGE TOO: STAGE B is the stage that BUILDS and INJECTS the per-chunk block, so it MUST apply the 40KB injection cap (arm a) HERE, after filtering chunk `i`'s rows to `$CHUNK_REVIEW_FILES_i` — cap the per-chunk filtered block at 40KB (the post-filter injection cap), so the cap binds at the injecting stage in `--all` and the prompt-size protection is not pinned to STAGE A, which never injects. The gate's reviewed-set-relevance requirement (arm c) and the single-empty-block fallback (arm d) ALSO apply HERE per chunk — if, after filtering to `$CHUNK_REVIEW_FILES_i`, chunk `i` has NO matching coverage row, inject the EMPTY block `<coverage-artifacts></coverage-artifacts>` for THAT chunk so its test-sufficiency agent hits skip-and-note (D-02) for that chunk. (Note the STAGE-A vs STAGE-B division of the size protections: STAGE A owns the (a0) raw pre-parse size guard / non-resolving XML parse on the on-disk files; the assembling stage — diff-mode STAGE A or `--all` STAGE B — owns the 40KB post-filter injection cap (arm a).) The per-chunk filter REUSES the SAME `$CHUNK_REVIEW_FILES_i` Site C step 2 binds for the chunk's `<changed-files>`/`<files>` halves — reuse that list, do NOT recompute scope. NOTE: in DIFF-MODE there are no chunks and no Site C loop, so there is NO STAGE-B split — STAGE A's gated repo-level dataset filtered to the diff's reviewed file set IS the block directly (arm c is the STAGE-A reviewed-diff match); do NOT over-engineer diff-mode. The shared `<diff>`/`<files>` block position is UNCHANGED by this filter (the filter only changes the test-sufficiency-only coverage block contents, never the shared block).

findings.title: Coverage gate makes test-sufficiency conditional, but tracecheck's deep-plain expectations still require the dispatch
findings.problem: The new step 3 removes `test-sufficiency` from a diff-mode deep run whenever `$TS_GATE_CASE` is `no-artifact`/`none-usable`, but the default expectations fixture that tracecheck loads was not updated: `scripts/tracecheck.py:59` loads `fixtures/mode-path-expectations.json`, whose `deep-plain` entries (batch 1 and batch 2, ~lines 189-195) still list `test-sufficiency` under `required_dispatches`, and `tracecheck.py:396-399` adds `R_NO_DISPATCH` for any required agent with no answered dispatch. A correctly-behaving diff-mode deep trace on a repo with no usable coverage artifact therefore now fails tracecheck with a missing test-sufficiency dispatch. `deep-all` entries are unaffected. The fixture's own notes call test-sufficiency an 'always-on dispatch', which this diff makes untrue. Assumption: measurement traces run deep-plain on repos without coverage. pending: confirm the measurement fixtures/repos lack a usable coverage artifact.
findings.current_code: Otherwise, if the carried `$TS_GATE_CASE` (bound by Phase 1d, `01d-coverage.md`) is `no-artifact` or `none-usable`, REMOVE `test-sufficiency` from the set AND bind `$TS_GATED=<that case>`

findings.why_it_matters: The trace checker will flag correct gated runs as failures, corrupting measurement/verification results for deep-plain.
source_window: **Subtract `$CONFIG_DISABLED` from THIS deep Selection set BEFORE dispatch (config `disabled` → dispatch, parallel to `/review`'s `20-dispatch.md`).** The `disabled` roster was ALREADY resolved ONCE in Phase 0.6 (carried as `$CONFIG_DISABLED`) — deep-review does NOT re-read `config.py`; it consumes the carried-forward var. After this deep table produces its selected agent set (which adds `architecture`+`impact`+`test-sufficiency` to the universal floor; in diff mode `test-sufficiency` is subject to the coverage gate below) and BEFORE the dispatch announcement / fan-out, REMOVE any agent whose name ∈ `$CONFIG_DISABLED` from the set, so the disabled agents never dispatch and `score.py` never sees them. **Same LOCKED policy as `/review`:** HONOR any disable including a core agent (`bugs`/`security`); when `bugs` or `security` is disabled, APPEND the fixed-string `⚠ config: core agent '<name>' disabled — coverage reduced` announcement to the Phase-4 config-health warnings (never silent). A disabled deep-only agent (`architecture`/`impact`/`test-sufficiency`) or non-core agent is subtracted silently. In `--all` mode the subtraction applies inside EACH chunk's per-chunk deep fan-out (Site C) the same way (the roster is run-level). **Nothing else in config needs a deep-only touch:** `thresholds`, `min_confidence`, `idiom_floor`, the `// vibe-ignore` marker, and the Suppression (audit) and Low / Informational renders are resolved at Phase 0.6 (`06-config.md`) and applied at Phase 3 (`30-collect-score.md`) and Phase 4 (`40-render.md`) — the same shared files `/review` reads — so `/deep-review` adds NO config read and NO envelope key of its own. Only `top_model` and `disabled` are consumed here.

**DIFF-MODE COVERAGE GATE — remove `test-sufficiency` AFTER the `$CONFIG_DISABLED` subtraction and BEFORE the dispatch announcement (GATE-01).** The Selection table above is the candidate set and stays as it is; this paragraph is the ONE place `test-sufficiency` is removed on evidence.
